title: Gluing derived objects along a continuous ordinal open cover
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\lambda$ be a set-sized ordinal, and let $(W_\alpha)_{\alpha<\lambda}$ be an increasing family of open subsets with $X=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}W_\alpha$ and $W_\alpha=\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}W_\beta$ at every non-successor ordinal $\alpha<\lambda$ (in particular $W_0=\varnothing$ when $\lambda>0$). Suppose $K_\alpha\in D(\mathcal O_{W_\alpha})$ [def-pc-derived-category] and $\operatorname{Hom}(K_\alpha,K_\alpha[i])=0$ for every integer $i<0$. Suppose isomorphisms $r_\beta^\alpha:K_\alpha|_{W_\beta}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_\beta$ are given for all $\beta<\alpha<\lambda$ and satisfy $r_\gamma^\alpha=r_\gamma^\beta\circ(r_\beta^\alpha|_{W_\gamma})$ for $\gamma<\beta<\alpha$. Then there are $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and isomorphisms $r_\alpha:K|_{W_\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_\alpha$ such that $r_\beta^\alpha\circ(r_\alpha|_{W_\beta})=r_\beta$ for all $\beta<\alpha<\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union), specialized to the ringed space of a scheme.

proof.text: If $\lambda=0$, the covering equation gives $X=\varnothing$, and the zero complex is the required object. Hence assume $\lambda>0$. Regard each open as its open subscheme with the restricted structure sheaf. The site of its open subsets is small, since the opens form a subset of the power set of its underlying set. Every object of the derived category is represented by a complex, and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on this site supplies a K-injective representative $I_\alpha$ of $K_\alpha$. Fix these identifications. Restriction to any smaller open is exact by [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact] and preserves K-injectives by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open]. The exact-functor theorem [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] identifies termwise restriction with derived restriction, including shifts. We will construct chain maps $f_{\beta\alpha}:I_\beta\to I_\alpha|_{W_\beta}$ representing $(r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}$ and satisfying the strict equation $f_{\gamma\alpha}=(f_{\beta\alpha}|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B (lemma-glueing-increasing-union), first paragraph; K-injective existence as in Tag 071B; restriction Tag 08BS

proof.text: For an open inclusion $j:V\hookrightarrow O$, use the normalized extension by zero of [lem-weil-pbc-module-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Its unit $G\to(j_!G)|_V$ induces the isomorphism on every stalk in $V$ specified in clause (3). It is therefore an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks]: the inverse of a bijective module map is module-linear. We identify this restriction with $G$ using that unit. Adjunction applies degreewise to chain maps, since its naturality carries the chain-map equation to the chain-map equation. For $W_\beta\subset W_\gamma\subset O$, a chain map $f_{\beta\gamma}$ consequently induces $T^O_{\beta\gamma}:j_{\beta,O,!}I_\beta\to j_{\gamma,O,!}I_\gamma$, whose adjoint is $f_{\beta\gamma}$ followed by the restricted unit for $j_{\gamma,O,!}$. Under the interior stalk identifications its stalk at $x\in W_\beta$ is $(f_{\beta\gamma})_x$. Naturality of the units and the adjunction bijection show that the strict equations for $f$ give $T^O_{\gamma\delta}T^O_{\beta\gamma}=T^O_{\beta\delta}$: both adjoints are the restricted unit followed by $(f_{\gamma\delta}|_{W_\beta})f_{\beta\gamma}$. Thus the already constructed maps define an actual diagram of complexes on every common ambient open $O$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, extension-by-zero transition maps; Sheaves Tag 00A7 (lemma-j-shriek-modules)

proof.text: We construct the $f_{\beta\alpha}$ by transfinite recursion. There are no incoming maps at $\alpha=0$; $W_0=\varnothing$. If $\alpha=\delta+1$, the complex $I_\alpha|_{W_\delta}$ is K-injective by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open]. The Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $(r_\delta^\alpha)^{-1}$ by a chain map $f_{\delta\alpha}$. For $\beta<\delta$ define $f_{\beta\alpha}=(f_{\delta\alpha}|_{W_\beta})f_{\beta\delta}$. The original cocycle gives $[f_{\beta\alpha}]=(r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}$, and the prior strict equations imply the new strict equations by associativity. This handles every successor without making independent, potentially incoherent choices for the earlier indices.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, successor step of the recursion

proof.text: Suppose $0<\alpha<\lambda$ is a limit and the strict system has been constructed below $\alpha$. Using Step 2 on $O=W_\alpha$, form the termwise colimit $C_\alpha=\varinjlim_{\beta<\alpha}j_{\beta,\alpha,!}I_\beta$. These module colimits exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; the differential is induced by the differentials of the diagram and squares to zero since its composite is zero on every coprojection. Restricting a coprojection and precomposing with the unit of Step 2 gives $s_\beta:I_\beta\to C_\alpha|_{W_\beta}$. The cocone equation and the definition of $T$ give the strict equation $s_\gamma=(s_\beta|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}$ for $\gamma<\beta<\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, non-successor step: definition of the termwise colimit and its coprojections

proof.text: Fix $x\in W_\beta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-filtered-colimit], degreewise the stalk of $C_\alpha$ is the colimit of the stalks of its diagram, with its indicated coprojections. The tail $\beta\le\gamma<\alpha$ gives the same colimit: a cocone on this tail extends to an earlier index by its map to $\max(\beta,\gamma)$, uniquely; the cocone equations verify this extension. By the normalized stalk formula of [lem-weil-pbc-module-extension-by-zero-adjunction], the tail is the diagram $(I_\gamma)_x$, and its transition maps are $(f_{\gamma\delta})_x$. They are quasi-isomorphisms: their derived classes are the given inverse isomorphisms, so their maps on cohomology sheaves are isomorphisms, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] identifies the kernels and images defining stalk cohomology with the stalks of those sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, stalk display for C and restriction to the tail; Modules Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian)

proof.text: Here is the cohomology calculation in that tail, using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. A cycle in the colimit complex is represented in some degree at one index; its differential is zero at some later index, so it is represented by a cycle there. A cycle which becomes a boundary is represented, together with a primitive, at a common later index where the boundary equation holds. Thus $H^n(\varinjlim_\gamma(I_\gamma)_x)=\varinjlim_\gamma H^n((I_\gamma)_x)$. Equivalently, apply exactness to the sequences of cycles, terms and boundaries. Since all transition maps on cohomology are isomorphisms, the canonical map from $H^n((I_\beta)_x)$ to this colimit is an isomorphism: an element at $\gamma\ge\beta$ is the image of its inverse under the transition isomorphism, and equality is tested at a common later index. Hence $(s_\beta)_x$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By stalkwise detection of exactness in [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], its induced maps on cohomology sheaves have zero kernel and cokernel; therefore $s_\beta$ is a quasi-isomorphism on $W_\beta$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, explanation after the stalk display: exactness of filtered colimits; Algebra Tag 00DB (lemma-directed-colimit-exact)

proof.text: The opens $W_\beta$ for $\beta<\alpha$ cover $W_\alpha$, by continuity. Their intersection is the smaller of the two opens, so they have the intersection-refinement property. On $W_\beta$ define $a_\beta=(r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}[s_\beta]^{-1}:C_\alpha|_{W_\beta}\to K_\alpha|_{W_\beta}$. For $\gamma<\beta$ the equations $s_\gamma=(s_\beta|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}$ and $(r_\gamma^\alpha)^{-1}=((r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}|_{W_\gamma})(r_\gamma^\beta)^{-1}$ give $a_\gamma=a_\beta|_{W_\gamma}$, since $[f_{\gamma\beta}]=(r_\gamma^\beta)^{-1}$. This also shows equality when two indices have the same open, so the family is well defined on the set of distinct opens. Both local objects are isomorphic to $K_\beta$, so their cross negative Hom groups vanish by the hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] to $M=C_\alpha$, $N=K_\alpha$ and this family, obtaining $a:C_\alpha\to K_\alpha$. Apply it to the inverse family to obtain $b$ in the reverse direction. Hom injectivity applied to $ba$ and $ab$ gives the identities, so $a$ is an isomorphism. This uses the uniqueness/Hom assertion, without assuming effectivity of the desired increasing-union descent.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, identification of C with K_alpha, using the uniqueness mechanism of Tags 0D66 and 0D68; corrects the printed reference to Tag 0D6A

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], represent the class $a:C_\alpha\to K_\alpha=QI_\alpha$ by a chain map $t:C_\alpha\to I_\alpha$. Put $f_{\beta\alpha}=(t|_{W_\beta})s_\beta$. Its derived class is $a_\beta[s_\beta]=(r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}$. Moreover $(f_{\beta\alpha}|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}=(t|_{W_\gamma})(s_\beta|_{W_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}=(t|_{W_\gamma})s_\gamma=f_{\gamma\alpha}$ as chain maps, by Step 4. Thus the recursion also closes at each nonzero limit. The morphism represented by t has direction $C_\alpha\to K_\alpha$, which is the direction needed to compose the coprojections into $I_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, choice of tau and definition of the new transition maps; comparison direction corrected

proof.text: After this recursion, Step 2 on $O=X$ supplies a strict diagram $j_{\alpha,X,!}I_\alpha$, $\alpha<\lambda$. Set $L=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\lambda}j_{\alpha,X,!}I_\alpha$ termwise, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], and write $s_\alpha:I_\alpha\to L|_{W_\alpha}$ for its restricted coprojections. They satisfy $s_\beta=(s_\alpha|_{W_\beta})f_{\beta\alpha}$. For each $x\in W_\alpha$ the tail $\alpha\le\gamma<\lambda$ is nonempty and filtered; its stalk diagram has the normalized terms $(I_\gamma)_x$ and quasi-isomorphism transitions. Apply exactly the calculation of Steps 5 and 6 to this diagram: stalks commute with this small filtered colimit, cohomology of its stalk complexes commutes with the colimit, and the map from the first term is a quasi-isomorphism. Stalkwise exactness then makes $s_\alpha$ a quasi-isomorphism. This argument includes a successor $\lambda$, when the tail may have a last element; continuity at the final index is not required.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, final colimit and its stalk verification

proof.text: Take $K=QL$ and let $r_\alpha=[s_\alpha]^{-1}:K|_{W_\alpha}\to K_\alpha$. Inverting the strict coprojection equation and using $[f_{\beta\alpha}]=(r_\beta^\alpha)^{-1}$ gives $r_\beta=r_\beta^\alpha\circ(r_\alpha|_{W_\beta})$, as required. The cases where all opens are empty, repeated opens, or $\lambda=1$ use the same equations (every module on the empty space is zero). No boundedness or quasi-coherence assumption has been used.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, concluding compatibility of the isomorphisms
